corpusSummary: Across 2026 studies, the corpus charts how large language models intersect social life: trust, fairness, governance, safety, and equity; AI as methodological partners in education, health, policy, and humanities; patterns of human–AI interaction, adoption barriers, and social consequences; and heritage, culture, and literacy in AI-enabled futures. Together, they reveal opportunities for augmentation alongside concerns about reliability, bias, and cultural adequacy.

themes.name: Trust, ethics, governance, and safety
themes.description: Across health, education, policy, and corporate settings, studies examine how trust, equity, privacy, bias, and governance shape AI adoption, evaluation, and impact.

themes.name: AI as methodological tool and research collaborator
themes.description: A broad set of works demonstrates LLMs and related tools aiding analysis, coding, translation, simulation, and design, while emphasizing validation, transparency, and methodological caveats.

themes.name: Human–AI interaction, adoption dynamics, and social consequences
themes.description: Empirical work tracks how user perceptions of humanness, trust, social capital, and peer effects influence AI adoption, use, and social outcomes across education, health, work, and everyday life.

themes.name: Education, literacy, culture, and heritage in AI-enabled futures
themes.description: Research explores AI's role in learning, literacy for diverse populations, health education, and culturally grounded heritage and religious practices, balancing opportunities with ethics and cultural sensitivity.
